Published as Candidate, Unreviewed, significance 40.

Thank you for sending this. Haibin Hang's paper was read in full in its arXiv source on 19 November, and the conjecture was read in Murakami and Murakami's own paper: it is stated there for any knot, with the simplicial volume, so a knot for which the limit does not exist is a counterexample to it as written.

Because the claim is a big one for a five-page paper, a check was run here. The cabling sum from the paper was evaluated in high-precision integer arithmetic near the root of unity, after testing the formula on the unknot, the trefoil and the figure-eight knot. For the (1,2)-cable of the sum of two figure-eight knots the growth rate comes out at 4.186 for N = 1001 and 2.113 for N = 1000, where one figure-eight volume corresponds to 2.093 at that N; the (1,3)-cable shows the same split between N = 601 and N = 603, and the cable of a single figure-eight knot shows no split, as Le and Tran proved. That is what the theorem predicts. It is evidence at finite N, not a proof, so the tier is Unreviewed and the verification note opens with the sentence used for all major claims: no independent mathematician has checked this yet.

What was changed: the name and statement now give the conjecture as Murakami and Murakami posed it (the paper's phrase "all-knot volume conjecture" is kept in the address only); the year is 1999, when it was posted; the result note says what survives, namely the upper limit and the hyperbolic case, which is your point about the classic conjecture; a typo in the result note ("bcoprime") is gone; the model is recorded as OpenAI Codex, and the AI role quotes the paper's one sentence.

The mathematics was not changed. Corrections are welcome.

edits.name: The volume conjecture for all knots (Murakami and Murakami): does $\frac{2\pi}{N}\log|J_N(K;e^{2\pi i/N})|$ converge to the simplicial volume?
edits.field: Quantum topology; colored Jones polynomial, volume conjecture
edits.statement: Let $J_N(K;q)$ be the $N$-colored Jones polynomial of a knot $K$, normalized to be $1$ on the unknot, and put $R_N(K)=\frac{2\pi}{N}\log|J_N(K;e^{2\pi i/N})|$. Kashaev conjectured that for a hyperbolic knot this growth rate tends to the hyperbolic volume of the complement. Murakami and Murakami identified Kashaev's invariant with this evaluation of the colored Jones polynomial and proposed a stronger volume conjecture for any knot $K$: $$\lim_{N\to\infty}R_N(K)=v_3\,\|K\|,$$ where $\|K\|$ is the simplicial volume (Gromov norm) of the knot complement and $v_3$ is the volume of the regular ideal tetrahedron. The right side is the sum of the hyperbolic volumes of the JSJ pieces of the knot exterior. Does the limit exist and equal this volume for every knot, satellite knots included?
edits.posedBy: Hitoshi Murakami and Jun Murakami, The colored Jones polynomials and the simplicial volume of a knot, Acta Math. 186 (2001), 85-104, Conjecture 5.1
edits.ageNote: Posted to arXiv in May 1999 (math/9905075) and published in Acta Mathematica in 2001; it extends Kashaev's conjecture for hyperbolic knots. Le and Tran (2010) proved the limit for the (p,2)-cables of the figure-eight knot and found parity effects for cable links.
edits.resultNote: Theorem 1 of arXiv:2611.09063 (Haibin Hang, v1 6 November 2026): let $E$ be the figure-eight knot with volume $V$ and $L=C_{p,w}(E^{\#d})$ the $(p,w)$-cable of the connected sum of $d\ge2$ copies of $E$, with $w\ge2$ and $\gcd(p,w)=1$. Then the JSJ volume of $L$ is $dV$, $R_N(L)\to dV$ along $N$ coprime to $2w$, and $\limsup R_N(L)\le V$ along $N$ with $\gcd(N,w)>1$, so $\lim_N R_N(L)$ does not exist. For the $(1,2)$-cable of $E\#E$ the odd colors give $2V$ and the even colors at most $V$; for the $(1,3)$-cable the limit fails even along odd $N$. What survives: $\limsup_N R_N(L)=dV$ still equals the volume for these knots, and Kashaev's conjecture for hyperbolic knots is untouched, since the examples are satellite knots. The paper is 5 pages and rests on the Morton-van der Veen cabling formula, the Habiro-Le formula for the figure-eight knot and a derivative estimate at the root of unity.
edits.aiRole: The paper's acknowledgment, in full: "OpenAI Codex assisted with developing and checking the argument and preparing the manuscript." The paper does not say which steps came from the model or which model version was used.
edits.verificationNote: No independent mathematician has checked this yet. Read by this site on 19 November 2026 in the TeX source of arXiv:2611.09063v1 (single author, Haibin Hang, no affiliation given): the whole 5-page paper with its AI acknowledgment, and the volume conjecture in the source of Murakami and Murakami's arXiv:math/9905075, which is stated for any knot and matches. A sanity computation was written and run here, independent of the paper's estimates: the paper's cabling sum with the Habiro-Le formula, in high-precision fixed-point integer arithmetic close to the root of unity, after checking the formula on the unknot, on the trefoil as a cable and on the Jones polynomial of the figure-eight knot. For the $(1,2)$-cable of $E\#E$ it gives $R_{1001}=4.186$ and $R_{1000}=2.113$, against $\frac{2\pi}{N}\log J_N(E)=2.093$ at both; for the $(1,3)$-cable $R_{601}=4.255$ and $R_{603}=2.161$; the control $(1,2)$-cable of $E$ gives $2.109$ at both parities. This agrees with the theorem at finite $N$ but proves nothing about the limit, and it takes the cabling formula and the JSJ volume from the paper and the literature. The proof was not refereed; a web search found no public expert reaction.
edits.significanceNote: The volume conjecture is one of the central open problems of quantum topology, and the Murakami-Murakami form for all knots is the version usually quoted. What fails here is the existence of the limit for certain satellite knots: the upper limit still gives the volume and the hyperbolic case is untouched, so the score is for the all-knots extension, not for the conjecture's hyperbolic core. Below the purely cosmetic surgery conjecture (45) and the Kervaire conjecture (55); well above the mod 4 Kawauchi conjecture (20).
